landing_links.text:
Chapter 2: Musculoskeletal Modeling Conventions

Explains how anatomical calibration and frame definitions affect reported joint motion and inertial parameters. A declared ZXY example makes angle signs, branches and singularities explicit. Point-transport identities check spatial inertia and connect motion to kinetic energy and generalized loads.

For a golf swing, consistent conventions help distinguish changes of coordinates from changes in movement. They do not identify individual muscle forces or a neural control strategy. The chapter relates frame choices to the uncertainty in body-segment parameters and to the assumptions needed for biological inference.

Verification boundary: the printed code and manufactured examples check the declared mathematical conventions. Clinical side/sign mapping requires separate anatomical calibration.
